cases.prompt: I own this PDF and asked for a metadata-only cleanup. The cleaned copy is now structurally invalid. Preserve the evidence, determine what sanitation actually happened, then find why the cleaning tool corrupted the file.
cases.primary_decision: Establish the authorized sanitation result and artifact evidence before causal tool debugging.
cases.anti_route: Do not keep applying broader cleanup options or treat the corruption as proof that the metadata target was removed.

cases.prompt: The refactor scope and approval are already settled. Apply the approved slices, but keep an explicit definition of done so every slice, every invariant, and every final count is proven on the finished code before you report success.
cases.primary_decision: The refactor specialist owns what may change; completion-proof derives its done contract from the approved slices and proves each clause on the final candidate.
cases.anti_route: Do not let completion pressure expand the approved refactor or bypass its behavior-parity constraints.

cases.prompt: We do not have a known bug yet. Hunt this provider subsystem for hidden correctness defects, prove the strongest candidates, then take any confirmed candidate whose cause is still uncertain through causal diagnosis.
cases.primary_decision: Bug Finder owns unknown-defect discovery and proof; Debugging Investigator begins only after a concrete confirmed symptom needs causal explanation.
cases.anti_route: Do not start causal debugging before there is a specific failure candidate, and do not call suspicious code a confirmed bug without an observable contract violation.

cases.prompt: The repository test command cannot start because PowerShell selects a blocked package-manager shim. Establish one supported invocation first; after it runs, investigate the reproducible stale-total failure the tests expose.
cases.primary_decision: Toolchain Preflight owns reaching the real test path; Debugging Investigator begins only after that stable invocation exposes a concrete application failure.
cases.anti_route: Do not treat shell policy as the application's root cause, and do not keep preflight active once the supported test command runs.

cases.prompt: Review a Rust parser PR for regressions without editing. If I later approve a specific explained fix, implement that fix without renaming APIs or changing accepted inputs.
cases.primary_decision: The reviewer owns finding admission and remains read-only; Rust implementation starts only when the concrete fix is authorized.
cases.anti_route: Do not trigger the implementation specialist merely because the review contains Rust, or treat a review request as edit authority.

cases.prompt: Migrate our live Python service to Rust with rollback and a compatibility window. Once the transition stage is defined, implement only its bounded byte-processing module in Rust.
cases.primary_decision: Evolution owns consumers, rollout, and retirement criteria; Rust Engineering owns the bounded implementation handed over with those constraints.
cases.anti_route: Do not bypass the transition contract by treating a whole service replacement as a local port.

cases.prompt: Our Rust task leaks a permit when cancelled, but we do not yet know where. Reproduce and explain it, then implement the established fix and verify the affected state transitions.
cases.primary_decision: Diagnosis establishes the failing lifecycle boundary before the Rust implementation stage.
cases.anti_route: Do not start runtime redesign or add Send bounds as a speculative remedy for an unexplained failure.

cases.prompt: Review this PR. Most of it is a refactor, but the changed authorization helper now decides whether users can access other tenants' invoices. Focus on whether the new trust boundary is exploitable, then hand any non-security structural cleanup back to normal review.
cases.primary_decision: Security exploitability of the changed authorization boundary is primary; ordinary structural findings are secondary.
cases.anti_route: Do not let general refactor review dilute or replace the security-first authorization analysis.

cases.prompt: Review the defined kotlin change without editing, then implement only a specific explained fix after it is authorized.
cases.primary_decision: The reviewer admits findings; the language specialist receives a bounded authorized implementation with its protected contracts.
cases.anti_route: Do not turn the source language into implementation authority during a review-only stage.

cases.prompt: Plan a staged production transition to kotlin with compatibility and rollback, then implement its defined local package stage.
cases.primary_decision: Evolution owns staged consumer/deployment compatibility; the language specialist owns the bounded implementation stage.
cases.anti_route: Do not treat a whole product replacement as a local port or remove compatibility paths early.

cases.prompt: Implement a Flutter feature, including an already-defined Kotlin-only native plugin stage. Preserve Flutter behavior and hand over the bounded Android code with explicit contracts.
cases.primary_decision: Flutter owns feature integration; Kotlin owns only the handed-over native implementation stage.
cases.anti_route: Do not classify the whole Flutter feature as Kotlin work or reopen mobile platform selection.

cases.prompt: A Go service invokes a Python helper. The cause and exact remedy are established in the helper, and no Go source or wire changes are requested. Implement the helper remedy.
cases.primary_decision: The owned implementation is the Python helper; the caller's language does not take over.
cases.anti_route: Do not load Go implementation merely because a Go process launches the changed helper.

cases.prompt: Implement this specified C++ ownership correction in a bridge consumed by an unchanged Rust crate. Preserve its ABI and only edit the C++ side.
cases.primary_decision: C++ owns the changed native lifetime boundary and checks the Rust consumer contract.
cases.anti_route: Do not rewrite the Rust caller or make both language skills co-primary.
